Goad

GOHD (rhymes with road) · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To goad to prod, needle, or annoy someone into action, often through repeated teasing.

Classmates kept trying to goad her into arguing with the substitute teacher, but she just smiled and stayed quiet.

Worked Example

The rival team's captain spent the whole game shouting insults, clearly trying to goad their star player into a foul that would get him ejected.

The rival captain wasn't trying to have a real conversation -- he was deliberately needling and teasing to push someone into acting rashly. That repeated prodding toward an unwise reaction is exactly what goad means.

How Goad Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

prod

prod: to push or urge someone into action

taunt

taunt: to needle someone with mocking remarks

Antonyms

dissuade

dissuade: to persuade someone not to do something

soothe

soothe: to calm or gently comfort someone

How Strong Is It? — encourage → goad → torment

encourage vs. goad

encourage vs. goad: To encourage someone is a supportive, friendly nudge, without the mocking or needling edge of goading.

torment vs. goad

torment vs. goad: To torment someone is to cause them ongoing distress, a much harsher and more personal act than a single goading remark.

Build the Word

The pieces

whole word — goad

whole word — goad: originally a literal pointed stick used to prod cattle or oxen forward (Old English (gad))

Put it together

Put it together: Goad comes from an Old English word for a pointed stick used to poke and drive cattle forward. The literal image of jabbing an animal into moving stuck around as the figurative meaning of needling a person into action.

Use the root in a new word: goad (literal sense)

Use the root in a new word: goad (literal sense): Farmers once carried a long wooden goad to keep oxen moving steadily along the plow line.

Strength Check

Word Choice

Goad almost always implies a series of small, needling pushes rather than one single command -- and the person being goaded is often being pushed toward something unwise or reckless. Unlike galvanize, which excites a group toward a positive, energetic action, goad usually pushes one person toward something unwise, through teasing rather than inspiration.
